//: Pin the SDK so builds are reproducible, and so the lock files stay valid.
Some packages are referenced implicitly by the SDK rather than by any project file —
Microsoft.NET.ILLink.Tasks arrives because WinMux.Cli sets PublishSingleFile — and their
versions follow the SDK's patch level. With a floating SDK, packages.lock.json records a
version the next patch release changes, and a locked restore fails with NU1004 on a machine
that is merely more up to date. That is exactly what CI did the first time it ran.
rollForward is disabled rather than latestPatch for the same reason: allowing a newer patch
would reintroduce the drift the lock files exist to prevent. When the SDK is deliberately
updated, this file and the lock files change together, in one commit.
